To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a systematic development approach and modeling notation for service-oriented software systems.
We have developed a service modeling language, and we have developed an approach to systematically develop service-oriented software architectures.

(1) services are an appropriate modeling element for describing cross-cutting aspects of service-oriented architectures; (2) services and their mappings to target component configurations can be modeled using an architecture definition language; (3) services are an effective way of capturing cross-cutting aspects; and (4) the proposed architecture definition language and development process enable the systematic development and exploration of multiple service-oriented architectures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the systematic development of service-oriented software systems.
providing a comprehensive and systematic approach for the development and exploration of software architectures that are based on services.
the systematic development and exploration of software architectures based on services as crosscutting architectural aspects.

our approach is a step towards systematic development of service-oriented software systems.

our architecture definition language is expressive enough to model the service-oriented architecture of the Center TRAN automation system and that the process of modeling services in this language is not more complex than modeling other aspects of the system.
our approach enables systematic development of service-oriented architectures.

the proposed architecture definition language and development process provide a systematic way of modeling service-oriented architectures and exploring multiple architectures that provide the same services.
we have developed an approach for systematically developing and exploring service-oriented architectures.
the notion of service is a promising approach for the development of large-scale distributed software systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the notion of services can be used to systematically explore alternative software architectures for a given system.
services provide a powerful means for modeling cross-cutting concerns in large-scale distributed software systems.
services are not only a good implementation model for large-scale distributed, event-based systems, but also a good architectural model for the same systems.
